answers.question: What is the newsletter?
answers.answer: Weekly newsletter about personal finance for nurses, on Beehiiv.

answers.question: How big is it and how does it perform?
What are your rules?
answers.answer: I will not promote financial products I would not use myself and must disclose sponsors.

answers.question: What access do you have and where does data live?
answers.answer: Beehiiv access through the browser and exports. Keep data in a Google Sheet.

research.approach: Newsletter operators sell attention in a few separate ways and test each cheaply before leaning on one: sponsorships first because they need no new product, a paid tier as a distinct product rather than a paywalled copy of the free issue, and affiliate links only where the product truly fits. They know their numbers before pitching (subscribers, open rate, click rate, audience description), because sponsors price on those and on fit. They model revenue per stream with explicit assumptions instead of one hopeful total. Disclosure is built into the process: the label sits next to the sponsored item, in plain words, and not only at the bottom. A personal finance list for one profession adds a second rule, a written test for which products are acceptable, applied before any pitch goes out.

sources.title: Newsletter sponsorship rates 2026 (Creators Agency)
sources.note: Price each placement separately from a floor, the audience delivered and the outcome; name the denominator when quoting a CPM; opens can be inflated by Apple Mail Privacy Protection, so weight clicks. Agency blog, so a practitioner view, not a standard.

sources.title: Paved finds HR newsletter ad rates run 15 times higher than lifestyle lists (PPC Land)
sources.note: Q3 2026 prices per 1,000 subscribers by category: finance $7.11, health and wellness $5.60; priced per subscriber, not per thousand impressions. The article itself notes errors in the report's table, so treat as a rough range.

sources.title: The State of Paid Newsletters 2026 (beehiiv)
sources.note: Platform median free-to-paid conversion 0.62% at a median $10 a month; top performers far higher; make paid a distinct product; annual plans; a cancel flow. Vendor data, so treat as a planning range.

sources.title: FTC: Endorsement Guides, what people are asking
sources.note: Page is undated and reflects the 2023 revision of the Guides; read 2026-11. Payment, free products and affiliate commissions are material connections; disclose near the endorsement in plain words such as ad or paid link, not only in a description or behind a link. Written for social media and websites; the newsletter case follows the same principle.

steps.name: Export the list and issue numbers and check them
steps.why: Sponsors and pricing rest on subscriber, open and click numbers that must be right.

steps.name: Learn what comparable newsletters earn and from what
steps.why: Rates and conversion differ by niche; a range with sources beats a guess.

steps.name: Find which revenue streams fit this audience and the owner's rules
steps.why: Not every stream fits nurses reading about money, or the owner's no-products rule.

steps.name: Model revenue by stream and rank the options
steps.why: $3,000 a month may need more than one stream, and each carries different risk.

steps.name: Write sponsor rules and the disclosure wording
steps.why: Trust and compliance are set before the first pitch, not after.

steps.name: Build the media kit and sponsor outreach
steps.why: Sponsors respond to clear numbers, audience description and terms.

steps.name: Test willingness to pay, then design the premium tier
steps.why: The owner does not know if readers would pay; ask before building.

steps.name: Go live one step at a time and read the money
steps.why: Each placement or tier is a live action; results are read monthly against the target.

pitfalls.text: Quoting an open rate that machine opens may inflate; sponsors then see weak clicks.
Paywalling part of the free issue instead of making paid a different product.
Planning on one hopeful conversion rate; the platform median is far below the top performers.
Disclosing a sponsor only at the end of an issue or in vague words.
Taking a sponsor first and checking fit after, which breaks reader trust.

hypotheses.statement: The 52% open rate overstates real engagement, so sponsors will see weaker clicks than expected.
hypotheses.test: Compare unique opens, unique clicks and 90-day activity from the export.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Click rate is low next to the open rate and many subscribers have no clicks in 90 days.
hypotheses.refute_if: Click rate and recent activity are strong.

hypotheses.statement: Sponsors alone can cover most of $3,000 a month at this list size.
hypotheses.test: Price one slot two ways from dated sources, then multiply by issues a month: per 1,000 subscribers (the Paved finance figure of about $7 gives roughly $58 for 8,100 readers) and per 1,000 opens at vendor CPM ranges of $25 to $150 (about 4,200 opens, roughly $105 to $630 an issue).
hypotheses.confirm_if: A realistic rate times four to five issues, with more than one slot an issue, reaches most of $3,000.
hypotheses.refute_if: Even the high end of sourced rates with one slot an issue falls well short.

hypotheses.statement: A paid tier can contribute meaningfully: at the platform median of 0.62% conversion and $10 a month, 8,100 readers is roughly 50 payers and about $500 a month; 2 to 5% would be roughly $1,600 to $4,000.
hypotheses.test: Run the reader survey, then compare answers with the sourced conversion range.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Enough readers say they would pay and name a price near $10 or more.
hypotheses.refute_if: Few say they would pay or the price they name is far below $10.

hypotheses.statement: Some common stream, such as affiliate links for financial products, conflicts with the owner's rule and would cost reader trust.
hypotheses.test: Check each candidate stream and sponsor against the written rule.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Most candidates in the stream fail the rule.

hypotheses.statement: A few topics or links get most clicks, so sponsors in those spots would convert better.
hypotheses.test: Clicks by topic and link in the issue export.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Clicks concentrate on a few topics.

measurement.window: Read revenue monthly for six months; read each sponsor slot after its issue has had a full week of clicks; read the survey after enough answers have arrived.
measurement.min_volume: No paid-tier decision from fewer survey answers than the survey plan sets; sponsor results are judged over at least three issues, not one.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop a sponsor or stream at once if it fails the owner's rule, if disclosure is missing, or if unsubscribes or complaints rise above the earlier baseline; otherwise finish the window.
